lead_headline: Arvada ADA Plan Shows 67–72% Compliance in Buildings and Parks; Right-of-Way Lags at 24%

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council held a single-item workshop on the city's Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Transition Plan, receiving a progress update from the Infrastructure Department. Staff reported significant compliance gains in city facilities (67%) and parks (72%), while the public right-of-way — particularly curb ramps — remains at roughly 24% compliance under newly adopted, more stringent standards. No formal votes were taken; council direction gathered at this workshop will be incorporated into a final plan for adoption later in 2026.

tonight_at_a_glance.synopsis: Council received a workshop briefing on Arvada's updated ADA Transition Plan, with staff reporting major progress in facilities and parks while acknowledging substantial remaining work on sidewalks, curb ramps, and pedestrian crossings.
highlights: City facilities now 67% ADA-compliant; parks at 72%, with more than 11,400 combined barriers removed since 2020
Public right-of-way curb ramps only 24% compliant under newly adopted, stricter PROWAG standards — about 2,300 of nearly 10,000 ramps re-inspected and cleared
Staff exploring formation of a community ADA advisory board; council urged moving quickly, potentially tying it to plan adoption
Council members pressed for detailed sidewalk gap data, better coordination with Jefferson County, and a more programmatic approach to accessible parking enforcement
Final updated ADA Transition Plan expected to return to council later in 2026 for formal adoption

presentations.topic: ADA Program and ADA Transition Plan Update
presentations.presenter_name: Eric Leuen, Anne Foster, Jaclyn Rhodess, Claudia (last name not stated in transcript)
presentations.presenter_role: Deputy Director of Infrastructure; ADA Coordinator; Director of Infrastructure; Unidentified staff member — City of Arvada Infrastructure Department
prose_paragraphs: Staff from the Infrastructure Department presented an update on Arvada's ADA Transition Plan, which began in 2020 with a comprehensive citywide accessibility evaluation conducted in partnership with Meeting the Challenge. The evaluation identified approximately 4,800 barriers in city facilities (now 67% resolved), more than 11,000 barriers in the park system (now 72% resolved), and nearly 10,000 curb ramps in the public right-of-way, of which roughly 2,300 have been re-inspected and confirmed compliant (24%) using the more stringent Public Right-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines (PROWAG). Staff described a three-tier implementation strategy — near-term, mid-term, and long-term projects — and noted that dedicated ADA funding within each operational area allows rapid response to grievances, citing a curb ramp at 80th and Gray repaired within approximately one month of a resident complaint. The presentation sought council feedback before staff finalizes the plan for formal adoption later in 2026.
